_comment: MCP servers this kit knows how to work with. Claude Code reads this file when it
starts in this directory; other clients want the same block under a different name.
Nothing here is required. The kit runs end to end — crawl, write, review, publish,
render video — with none of it connected. These servers add the measurement half:
what the published work actually did once it was out.
NO CREDENTIALS LIVE HERE. Every server below authenticates over OAuth in your client
(`/mcp` in Claude Code). Pipeboard never receives your Meta, Google or TikTok password,
and this repo never sees a token. That is the same env-only rule the scripts follow:
no secret is ever written to a file that git can see.
Remove a block you do not use. An unreachable server is one more thing failing at

_note_ads: Pipeboard — hosted remote MCP for ad platforms. Free plan, OAuth, badged Meta
Business Partner. Its own code is Business Source License 1.1 (becomes Apache-2.0
in 2029), i.e. source-available rather than open source. That does not affect you
as a user of the hosted service, but this kit says so rather than implying every
connection it suggests is MIT like the rest.
These are READ-AND-WRITE: the same connection that reads spend can change a budget
or pause a campaign. Ask for a plan before letting an agent act on a live account.
